statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. The latest accessible NQ quote page still reflects the September 3 session rather than a verified reopened price path; Tail therefore remains below the blocking threshold while payroll and Middle East energy risk keep Stress extreme.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH. The next material escalation checkpoint is the observed price path after the 12:30 UTC Employment Situation; persistent extension with shallow or failed retracements would raise Tail, while orderly two-sided discovery would support normalization.
headline: Tail stays at WATCH overnight; Friday payrolls define the next conditional risk window
body: U.S. equities closed sharply higher on September 3, with the Nasdaq Composite up 1.40% and broad positive breadth after Governor Waller's remarks helped ease rate-hike fears. Oil remained near six-week highs amid Middle East supply risk. Fresh reopened NQ structure is not independently verified, and shared Finviz context is stale beyond its 90-minute limit.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 UTC clock-hours, Tail was low through the overnight and European sessions, moved to WATCH around the U.S. event and opening window, became elevated during the late technology-led rally, and returned to WATCH after the close as the rally retraced from its extreme and fresh reopened continuation could not be verified.
outlookSummary: Current Tail remains WATCH because the prior U.S. trend ended off its extreme and fresh reopened NQ persistence is not independently verified. Overnight Tail can normalize absent renewed directional efficiency. Payrolls keeps Stress extreme; any elevated post-release Tail is conditional on observed persistent extension, failed retracements or session-extreme holding.

forecast.analysis: Absent persistent extension through the Asian session, Tail can slip below WATCH even as payroll proximity keeps Stress near extreme.
A balanced overnight range with ordinary retracements would keep Tail low; a clean directional break that survives pullbacks would challenge this path.
Pre-Europe conditions favor low Tail if two-sided rotation persists. Stress remains elevated by the approaching labor report and unresolved energy risk.
The Asia-to-Europe handoff can raise sensitivity without implying a pathological path; Tail stays low unless direction persists across the liquidity transition.
European liquidity would test whether overnight direction is durable. Tail remains low unless price holds near an extreme and retracements repeatedly fail.
As Europe becomes fully active, Tail returns to WATCH if directional pressure broadens; ordinary counter-moves would cap the path risk.
The Europe-U.S. transition increases event sensitivity, but no pre-release alignment is assumed. Tail remains WATCH unless actual structure becomes persistently one-way.
U.S. premarket liquidity and payroll positioning can widen swings. Tail remains below the blocking threshold because the release outcome and post-release path are still unknown.
With the labor report two hours away, Stress is extreme while Tail stays WATCH. Only observed persistent repricing, not the scheduled release itself, would justify escalation.
drivers: Observed path required for Tail escalation

forecast.analysis: The final pre-release hour carries high whipsaw risk, but Tail remains WATCH unless live structure already shows shallow pullbacks or repeated extension.

The 12:30 UTC Employment Situation falls inside this hour. Tail is capped at WATCH before the print; any higher state depends on subsequently observed persistence, failed retracements, and cross-asset alignment.
After payrolls, elevated Tail is conditional on one-way repricing surviving meaningful retracements. Orderly two-sided price discovery would invalidate the elevated scenario quickly.

The first full U.S. cash-market hour has the highest conditional Tail in the forecast: sustained opening-auction continuation and failed pullbacks would support it, while rapid mean reversion would lower it.
Elevated Tail persists only if the post-release move keeps extending without meaningful counter-swings. Stabilizing yields and broader two-sided trade would argue for faster normalization.
Tail sits at the bottom of the elevated band conditionally. A durable retracement or volatility decay would move the regime back toward WATCH.
By late U.S. morning, Tail falls back to WATCH if price discovery becomes two-sided. Renewed extension after a failed retracement would be the main contrary signal.
Afternoon risk stays at WATCH while the market digests payrolls. Tail remains below blocking unless a fresh directional leg develops with little mean reversion.
Later afternoon conditions favor WATCH if volatility and directional efficiency ease; persistent session-extreme holding would keep path risk elevated.
Into the late U.S. session, Tail remains WATCH unless price again compresses near an extreme and then extends without meaningful retracement.
Toward the weekly close, Tail can return to low if event-driven structure has normalized. Residual headline risk keeps Stress high even without an active one-way path.
After regular Friday price discovery fades, Tail remains low absent a new market-moving headline; Stress still reflects unresolved macro and energy uncertainty.
The final forecast hour keeps Tail low because no persistent live path is assumed after the weekly session. Geopolitical developments remain the main residual discontinuity risk.
